Им объясняют нынешнюю ситуацию или видимый результат — кто-то устал, промок или испачкался из-за недавнего действия.

I'm tired because I've been running. — Я устал, потому что бегал.
Your eyes are red. Have you been crying? — У тебя красные глаза. Ты плакал?
The ground is wet — it's been raining. — Земля мокрая — шёл дождь.

pitfalls.en: Do not drop "been": "I have been working", NOT "I have working".
pitfalls.ru: Не теряй «been»: «I have been working», а не «I have working».

pitfalls.en: Only the main verb takes -ing: "have been doing", not "have been did".
pitfalls.ru: Окончание -ing только у смыслового глагола: «have been doing», а не «have been did».

pitfalls.en: State verbs (know, like, be) usually stay simple: "I have known her for years", not "I have been knowing".
pitfalls.ru: Глаголы состояния (know, like, be) обычно в простой форме: «I have known her for years», а не «I have been knowing».

summary.en: When you report a question, use normal word order (no do/does/did) and "if"/"whether" for yes/no questions. To report an order or request, use "tell/ask someone to + verb".
summary.ru: В косвенном вопросе — обычный порядок слов (без do/does/did) и «if»/«whether» для да/нет-вопросов. Чтобы передать приказ или просьбу — «tell/ask someone to + глагол».

text.en:
Keep the question word (where, what, why…), then use normal word order — subject before verb — and no do/does/did. The verb usually backshifts.

"Where do you live?" → He asked where I lived.
"What time does it start?" → She asked what time it started.
text.ru:
Сохрани вопросительное слово (where, what, why…), затем обычный порядок — подлежащее перед глаголом — и без do/does/did. Глагол обычно сдвигается назад.

"Where do you live?" → He asked where I lived.
"What time does it start?" → She asked what time it started.

examples.en: "Why are you sad?" → She asked why I was sad.
examples.ru: «Почему ты грустишь?» → Она спросила, почему я грущу.

text.en:
For a yes/no question, join it with "if" or "whether" and again use normal word order.

"Are you ready?" → She asked if I was ready.
"Do you like it?" → He asked whether I liked it.
text.ru:
Для да/нет-вопроса используй «if» или «whether» и снова обычный порядок слов.

"Are you ready?" → She asked if I was ready.
"Do you like it?" → He asked whether I liked it.

examples.en: "Can you swim?" → He asked if I could swim.
examples.ru: «Ты умеешь плавать?» → Он спросил, умею ли я плавать.

text.en:
To report an order or a request, use "tell/ask + person + to + verb". For a negative, put "not" before "to".

"Wait here." → She told me to wait.
"Please help." → He asked me to help.
"Don't be late." → She told us not to be late.
text.ru:
Чтобы передать приказ или просьбу — «tell/ask + человек + to + глагол». Для отрицания ставь «not» перед «to».

"Wait here." → She told me to wait.
"Please help." → He asked me to help.
"Don't be late." → She told us not to be late.

examples.en: "Sit down." → The teacher told us to sit down.

pitfalls.en: No do/does/did and normal order: "where I lived", not "where did I live".
pitfalls.ru: Без do/does/did и обычный порядок: «where I lived», а не «where did I live».

pitfalls.en: Commands use "to + verb", not "that": "told me to wait", not "told me that wait".
pitfalls.ru: Приказы — «to + глагол», не «that»: «told me to wait», а не «told me that wait».

pitfalls.en: Negative command: "not to" before the verb: "told us not to be late".
pitfalls.ru: Отрицательный приказ: «not to» перед глаголом: «told us not to be late».

title.en: Modals of deduction (must / can't / might be)

summary.en: Modal verbs let you say how sure you are about a situation. "must" = you are almost certain it is true; "can't" = almost certain it is not; "might/may/could" = it is possible. For the past, add "have + V3".
summary.ru: Модальные глаголы показывают, насколько ты уверен в ситуации. «must» = почти уверен, что так; «can't» = почти уверен, что не так; «might/may/could» = возможно. Для прошлого добавь «have + V3».

text.en:
Use the bare verb after the modal. "must" for a confident yes, "can't" for a confident no, and "might/may/could" for a possibility.

The lights are on — he must be home.
She just ate — she can't be hungry.
He isn't answering — he might be busy.
text.ru:
После модального — «голый» глагол. «must» — уверенное «да», «can't» — уверенное «нет», «might/may/could» — возможность.

The lights are on — he must be home.
She just ate — she can't be hungry.
He isn't answering — he might be busy.

examples.en: You've worked all day — you must be tired.
examples.ru: Ты работал весь день — ты, наверное, устал.

text.en:
For "I'm sure it isn't true", use "can't", NOT "mustn't". "mustn't" means "it is forbidden", which is completely different.

That can't be right. (I'm sure it's wrong)
You mustn't park here. (it's forbidden — different meaning)
text.ru:
Для «я уверен, что это не так» — «can't», а НЕ «mustn't». «mustn't» значит «запрещено» — совсем другое.

That can't be right. (уверен, что неверно)
You mustn't park here. (запрещено — другой смысл)

examples.en: He can't be forty — he looks so young!
examples.ru: Ему не может быть сорок — он такой молодой!

heading.en: Past: must / can't / might have + V3
heading.ru: Прошлое: must / can't / might have + V3

text.en:
To guess about the past, use modal + have + past participle.

The ground is wet — it must have rained.
He can't have seen me — I was hidden.
She might have missed the bus.

In speech "have" sounds like "of", but always write "must have", never "must of".
text.ru:
Чтобы догадываться о прошлом — модальный + have + причастие.

The ground is wet — it must have rained.
He can't have seen me — I was hidden.
She might have missed the bus.

В речи «have» звучит как «of», но пиши всегда «must have», не «must of».

examples.en: The cup is warm — he must have just left.
examples.ru: Чашка тёплая — он, должно быть, только что ушёл.

pitfalls.en: Confident "no" is "can't/can't have", not "mustn't": "She can't be serious".
pitfalls.ru: Уверенное «нет» — «can't/can't have», не «mustn't»: «She can't be serious».

pitfalls.en: Past deduction uses have + V3: "must have gone", not "must went" or "must of gone".
pitfalls.ru: Догадка о прошлом — have + V3: «must have gone», а не «must went» или «must of gone».

pitfalls.en: Bare verb after the modal: "must be", "might be" — not "must to be".
pitfalls.ru: «Голый» глагол после модального: «must be», «might be» — не «must to be».

summary.en: After one verb, you often need another verb — but should it be the -ing form or "to + verb"? The choice depends on the first verb. Some take -ing, some take "to", and a few take either.
summary.ru: После одного глагола часто нужен другой — но в какой форме, -ing или «to + глагол»? Выбор зависит от первого глагола. Одни требуют -ing, другие «to», немногие — любую.

text.en:
These verbs are followed by the -ing form: enjoy, mind, avoid, finish, keep, practise, suggest, imagine.

I enjoy cooking.
Would you mind waiting?
He suggested going out.
text.ru:
После этих глаголов идёт форма на -ing: enjoy, mind, avoid, finish, keep, practise, suggest, imagine.

I enjoy cooking.
Would you mind waiting?
He suggested going out.

examples.en: She kept talking for an hour.
examples.ru: Она говорила без остановки целый час.

text.en:
These verbs are followed by "to + verb": want, need, hope, decide, plan, promise, learn, offer, refuse, manage, agree, afford.

I want to learn Spanish.
They decided to move.
She offered to help.
text.ru:
После этих глаголов идёт «to + глагол»: want, need, hope, decide, plan, promise, learn, offer, refuse, manage, agree, afford.

I want to learn Spanish.
They decided to move.
She offered to help.

examples.en: We managed to catch the last train.
examples.ru: Нам удалось успеть на последний поезд.

heading.en: -ing as a noun and after prepositions

text.en:
Use the -ing form as the subject of a sentence, and ALWAYS after a preposition (in, at, of, before, instead of, worth).

Swimming is good for you.
She's good at drawing.
It's worth trying.
text.ru:
Используй форму на -ing как подлежащее и ВСЕГДА после предлога (in, at, of, before, instead of, worth).

Swimming is good for you.
She's good at drawing.
It's worth trying.

examples.en: I'm interested in learning to cook.

text.en:
With stop, remember, forget and try, the two forms mean different things.

He stopped smoking. (quit) — He stopped to smoke. (paused in order to)
Remember to lock the door. (a task) — I remember locking it. (a memory)
text.ru:
У stop, remember, forget, try две формы значат разное.

He stopped smoking. (бросил) — He stopped to smoke. (остановился, чтобы покурить)
Remember to lock the door. (дело) — I remember locking it. (воспоминание)

pitfalls.en: After a preposition, always use -ing: "good at cooking", not "good at to cook".
pitfalls.ru: После предлога — всегда -ing: «good at cooking», а не «good at to cook».

pitfalls.en: "want/decide/hope" take "to": "I want to go", not "I want going".
pitfalls.ru: «want/decide/hope» с «to»: «I want to go», а не «I want going».

pitfalls.en: "enjoy/avoid/suggest" take -ing: "enjoy reading", not "enjoy to read".
pitfalls.ru: «enjoy/avoid/suggest» с -ing: «enjoy reading», а не «enjoy to read».

title.en: Future forms extended (future continuous, be about to)
title.ru: Расширенные формы будущего (future continuous, be about to)

summary.en: Beyond will and going to, English has more ways to talk about the future: the future continuous for an action in progress, "be about to" for the very next moment, and the present simple for timetables.
summary.ru: Кроме will и going to, в английском есть и другие способы говорить о будущем: future continuous для действия в процессе, «be about to» для следующего мига и present simple для расписаний.

text.en:
Use it for an action that will be IN PROGRESS at a certain future time.

This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Rome.
At 8pm they'll be having dinner.
What will you be doing this evening?
text.ru:
Используй для действия, которое будет ИДТИ в определённый момент в будущем.

This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Rome.
At 8pm they'll be having dinner.
What will you be doing this evening?

examples.en: Don't call at nine — I'll be working.
examples.ru: Не звони в девять — я буду работать.

text.en:
Use it for something that will happen in the very next moment — stronger than "going to".

Hurry — the train is about to leave.
I'm just about to call you.
She was on the point of leaving. (= about to leave)
text.ru:
Используй для того, что произойдёт в следующий миг — настойчивее, чем «going to».

Hurry — the train is about to leave.
I'm just about to call you.
She was on the point of leaving. (= about to leave)

examples.en: Sit down — the film is about to start.

text.en:
For fixed schedules (trains, films, shops), use the present simple even about the future.

The train leaves at six.
The museum opens at ten.
What time does the film start?
text.ru:
Для чётких расписаний (поезда, фильмы, магазины) — present simple, даже о будущем.

The train leaves at six.
The museum opens at ten.
What time does the film start?

examples.en: Our flight departs at noon.

text.en: will = prediction or decision now; going to = plan or evidence; present continuous = arrangement; future continuous = in progress; be about to = the next moment; present simple = timetable.
text.ru: will = прогноз или решение сейчас; going to = план или признаки; present continuous = договорённость; future continuous = в процессе; be about to = следующий миг; present simple = расписание.

pitfalls.en: Keep "be" in the future continuous: "will be working", not "will working".
pitfalls.ru: Не теряй «be» в future continuous: «will be working», а не «will working».

pitfalls.en: "be about to" + bare verb: "about to leave", not "about to leaving".
pitfalls.ru: «be about to» + голый глагол: «about to leave», а не «about to leaving».

pitfalls.en: Timetables use present simple: "the train leaves at six", not "will leave".
pitfalls.ru: Расписания — present simple: «the train leaves at six», а не «will leave».
